features.description:
Define the canonical target-context prose prelude shape and capture regression fixtures from observed EC5 failure cases. Prelude shape (D001 — locked here): a markdown block at the top of the persisted `summary` field, before any other content. Format: `## Target context
- Repo: <repo>
- Env: <env>
- Project: <project_or_none>
- Command: <count> (see structured target_context.commands_run)

` followed by a blank line. Field order is fixed: Repo, Env, Project, Command. Labels are capitalized. All four lines are ALWAYS rendered — none are conditionally omitted. Project handling: when `target_context.project` is None / null / empty / the literal string 'none', the line renders as `- Project: (none)` (matches F023 plan.md `target_project: none` convention for host-local plans). Repo handling per D002 precedence: struct value first, cwd basename fallback, hard-fail on neither. Command (singular noun) shows the COUNT of `commands_run` + pointer to structured field — no list re-rendering. Fixtures live under `evidence/f001/fixtures/` as audit-envelope-shaped JSON files: `case-a-implementer-missing-prelude.json` (valid struct + commands_run present + summary lacking prelude → after F002, prelude injected; F003 classifier returns 'i0'), `case-b-auditor-self-finding.json` (auditor envelope missing prelude in its own summary; same outcome as case-a), `case-c-golden-valid-struct-valid-prelude.json` (no normalization needed; F003 classifier returns 'none'), `case-d-struct-absent.json` (no target_context key at all; F002 raises TargetContextError; F003 classifier returns 'i1'), `case-e-struct-invalid-empty-env.json` (target_context present but env=='' while commands_run non-empty; F002 raises; F003 'i1'), `case-f-commands-without-target.json` (commands_run non-empty AND env present BUT project absent or empty; F002 raises; F003 'i1'), and **`case-g-prelude-value-mismatch.json` (negative control)** — target_context validates with env=dev, project=<firebase-project-id>, commands_run non-empty, BUT the prose summary's prelude block has `Env: prod` (mismatch with struct's `dev`). This is the acceptance-narrowing case: F003 classifier MUST return 'i1' for this case (the auditor's finding is content-correctness, not format), demonstrating that downgrade is narrow — only missing/malformed prelude with valid struct, NOT any case where struct is valid. Each fixture carries a `_fixture_notes` field describing the exact failure shape, the originating real envelope (when sourced from an existing one), and the expected outcomes for both F002 (write-side) and F003 (classifier). Pure design + fixtures; no behavior change in this feature.
steps: Document the canonical prelude shape in `scripts/jarvis_orchestrate/target_context_prelude.py` as a module-level constant `PRELUDE_TEMPLATE: str` with `# format: <field-order-spec>` comment + a `render_prelude(target_context: dict) -> str` function that returns the rendered string. Pure function, no I/O, deterministic output.
Define `TargetContextError(ValueError)` with message format `'target_context invalid: <reason>'` for use by F002.

Define `validate_target_context(tc: dict | None) -> None` raising TargetContextError on the four invalid shapes (None/missing, env='' when commands_run non-empty, project='' when commands_run non-empty, commands_run non-empty AND env+project both absent). The helper is what F002 calls; F001 ships it as a pure function with tests.

Source the six fixtures from real recent envelopes — pick the smallest exemplar of each shape from the existing audit/ directories under docs/plans/. Verbatim except: (a) sanitize agent-specific identifiers (model_version → 'fixture-model-v1', agent → 'fixture-agent'), (b) strip findings[] (we want the envelope shape, not the finding list — F003 recomputes), (c) add `_fixture_notes` field describing the case.
Write fixtures to `evidence/f001/fixtures/` as the named files; commit alongside this feature.

Tests: `test_target_context_prelude.py` covers (a) `render_prelude` produces the documented format byte-for-byte for a known input (golden test), (b) deterministic output across calls (idempotence), (c) `validate_target_context` raises on each of the four invalid shapes (parametrized), (d) `validate_target_context` returns None on the two valid shapes (case-a-style and case-c-style), (e) every fixture file in `evidence/f001/fixtures/` parses as JSON and has the expected `_fixture_notes` describing its case.
features.acceptance: (1) `scripts/jarvis_orchestrate/target_context_prelude.py` exists with `PRELUDE_TEMPLATE`, `render_prelude(tc)`, `validate_target_context(tc)`, `parse_prelude_block(summary) -> dict | None`, and `TargetContextError` exported. (2) `render_prelude` is a pure function — no I/O, no logging — and produces deterministic output (assertion: 100 calls with same input return identical strings). (3) `PRELUDE_TEMPLATE` matches D001 format byte-for-byte: 4 lines (Repo, Env, Project, Command) with capitalized labels, fixed order, and trailing blank line. Module docstring cites D001 + D002. (4) Repo precedence (D002): `render_prelude` resolves repo from struct first, then `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` basename, then raises TargetContextError if neither yields a value. The cwd-fallback is documented in the module as a transitional shim. (5) Project rendering: when `target_context.project` is None / null / '' / 'none', the line renders as `- Project: (none)`; otherwise the literal value. Verified by parametrized golden test. (6) `validate_target_context` raises `TargetContextError` for all four invalid shapes (missing/None target_context, empty env with commands, empty project with commands, commands-without-env-or-project) — verified by parametrized tests. (7) `parse_prelude_block(summary)` returns a `{repo, env, project, command_count}` dict when the summary's leading block matches the canonical format; returns `None` when no prelude block is detectable; raises only on parse-shape mismatches that look like preludes (e.g. wrong field order, mistyped labels). (8) **Seven fixture files** land under `evidence/f001/fixtures/` with the names: `case-a-implementer-missing-prelude.json`, `case-b-auditor-self-finding.json`, `case-c-golden-valid-struct-valid-prelude.json`, `case-d-struct-absent.json`, `case-e-struct-invalid-empty-env.json`, `case-f-commands-without-target.json`, **`case-g-prelude-value-mismatch.json`**. (9) Each fixture carries a `_fixture_notes` field naming the case, the originating real envelope (where applicable), the expected F002 outcome (`prelude-injected` / `error-raised` / `no-change`), and the expected F003 classifier verdict (`'none'` / `'i0'` / `'i1'`). (10) Case-g specifically: target_context validates (env=dev, project=<firebase-project-id>, commands_run non-empty), summary's prelude block contains `- Env: prod` (mismatch with struct's dev). F002 outcome: `no-change` (prelude already present, idempotent no-op — F002 doesn't validate prose values). F003 verdict: `'i1'` (auditor-detected value mismatch, kept as blocker — narrow downgrade rule per D005). (11) Tests cover render-prelude golden output, idempotence, repo precedence (struct / cwd-fallback / hard-fail), project special-case rendering, validate-target-context parametrized invalid + valid shapes, parse_prelude_block parametrized over all 7 fixtures, and fixture-files-load smoke test. (12) No supervisor / audit_writer / auditor-prompt changes in this feature — F001 is design + fixtures + pure helpers only. (13) All existing orchestrate test modules stay green.

features.description: Implement the prelude-injection write-side fix in `audit_writer.py`. When the writer finalizes an envelope: (1) call `validate_target_context(envelope.target_context)` first — if it raises `TargetContextError`, the writer re-raises (with context: which envelope, which plan) and the envelope does NOT land on disk. This is a hard fail so the implementer must fix the structured side. (2) If validation passes, check whether the persisted `summary` already contains the canonical prelude (string-prefix match against the rendered prelude). If yes, no-op. If no, prepend `render_prelude(target_context)` to summary and persist. (3) Idempotence: re-finalizing an envelope (re-running supervisor with the same audit_id) produces a byte-identical result; the prelude is NOT injected twice. (4) Forward-only: no backfill of historical envelopes (D007). (5) Soft-degrade: if `target_context` field is entirely absent on a legacy envelope from before F023, the writer logs a deprecation warning + raises (matches case-d behavior). The change lives in audit_writer.py only; supervisor.py is unmodified — supervisor's pre-finalize hook calls audit_writer as today, audit_writer is now the gate. Tests use the F001 fixtures: case-a + case-b → prelude injected, summary written with prelude prepended, re-finalize round-trips identically; case-c → no-op, persisted summary unchanged byte-for-byte; case-d, case-e, case-f → TargetContextError raised, file does NOT land on disk (verified by Path.exists() == False after the writer call).
steps: Modify `audit_writer.py`: import `validate_target_context`, `render_prelude`, `TargetContextError` from `target_context_prelude`. Add a `_normalize_summary(envelope)` private function that does the validate → check-prefix → inject sequence. Call `_normalize_summary` at the top of the writer's persist function, before any disk I/O.

Idempotence detection: prelude prefix match uses `summary.lstrip().startswith(rendered_prelude.rstrip())` rather than full-string `startswith` so trailing-whitespace drift in the persisted file doesn't cause double-injection.

Error path: when `validate_target_context` raises, audit_writer wraps the error with `TargetContextError(f'envelope {envelope.audit_id} for plan {plan_id}: {orig_message}')` and re-raises. NO partial-write — the envelope file is not created at all.

Logging: the writer logs a single line at INFO when prelude is injected (`audit_writer: injected target-context prelude for {audit_id}`) and at WARNING when validation fails (so operators see why a volley aborted). No logging on the no-op case (case-c).

Tests — case-a positive: load case-a fixture, call audit_writer.persist with a tmp output dir, assert (i) the resulting file exists, (ii) the file's summary starts with the canonical prelude byte-for-byte, (iii) the rest of the summary is unchanged from the fixture, (iv) re-running persist on the resulting envelope produces a byte-identical file (idempotence).
Tests — case-b positive: same as case-a but using the auditor self-finding fixture; same assertions.
Tests — case-c golden no-op: load case-c fixture, persist, assert file content is byte-identical to fixture (the prelude was already there, no second injection).

Tests — case-d/e/f error paths: parametrized over the three invalid fixtures; for each, call persist with a tmp output dir, assert `TargetContextError` is raised, assert the output file does NOT exist (Path.exists() == False).
Tests — error-message context: the raised TargetContextError message contains both the audit_id and the plan_id, verified via regex.

Tests — supervisor integration: running a synthetic supervisor volley iteration end-to-end with case-a-shaped envelope produces a finalized envelope with the prelude injected; running with case-d-shaped envelope causes the supervisor to raise and exit non-zero (matches existing breaker error-path conventions).

Regression: existing `test_audit_writer.py` (and any other tests that exercise audit_writer) stay green. If tests were authored against pre-normalization behavior (envelopes whose summaries lacked prelude), they need fixture updates — call those out and adjust to use case-c-shaped fixtures.

(2) When struct validates and summary lacks prelude, `_normalize_summary` prepends `render_prelude(target_context)` to summary; the persisted file's summary starts with the canonical prelude byte-for-byte. (3) **Explicit idempotence proof** — at minimum two tests assert byte-equality: (3a) load case-c (already-canonical) fixture, persist to tmp_path, read back, assert resulting file's bytes equal the source fixture's bytes verbatim (no re-injection, no whitespace drift); (3b) double-persist test: persist case-a, capture resulting file bytes, persist the resulting envelope AGAIN to a different tmp_path, assert the second-pass output bytes equal the first-pass output bytes. The injected prelude is never doubled. (4) **Explicit forward-only proof** — at minimum one test: copy a real historical audit envelope from `docs/plans/*/audit/*.json` (one without the canonical prelude) into a tmp_path, run a synthetic supervisor cycle that does NOT call audit_writer.persist on it (e.g. read-only inspection), assert the file's bytes are unchanged. F002 must NOT walk historical envelopes; normalization applies only to envelopes flowing through `audit_writer.persist` going forward. Auditor verifies by reading the implementation: no glob walks of plan directories, no migration script, no rewrite of pre-existing files. (5) **Explicit no-partial-artifact proof** — at minimum three tests parametrized over case-d / case-e / case-f: (5a) call persist with a tmp_path; (5b) assert `TargetContextError` is raised; (5c) assert `Path(tmp_path / expected_filename).exists() == False` AFTER the raise (no half-written file, no zero-byte placeholder); (5d) assert no sibling/temp files exist in tmp_path either (e.g. no `.tmp` or `.partial` artifacts). The envelope path must be untouched on hard-fail. (6) Seven F001 fixtures each produce the documented outcome: case-a, case-b → prelude injected; case-c → no-op (byte-identical); **case-g → no-op (prelude already present; F002 does NOT validate prelude values, just presence — value mismatches are F003's classifier territory)**; case-d, case-e, case-f → TargetContextError raised, output file does NOT exist after the call. (7) Error messages contain both `audit_id` and `plan_id` (verified by regex test). (8) INFO log line on injection, WARNING log line on validation failure, no log on no-op — verified by capturing logger output in tests. (9) Synthetic supervisor integration test: case-a-shaped envelope round-trips through a real supervisor volley iteration with prelude injected; case-d-shaped envelope causes supervisor to raise + exit non-zero. (10) `audit.schema.json` is NOT modified (D006 records the schema-bump deferral). (11) Forward-only — no backfill of historical envelopes (D007 — no migration step, no walk-and-rewrite). (12) All existing orchestrate test modules stay green; any pre-normalization-era test that uses summaries-without-prelude as input is updated to use case-c-shaped fixtures (or rewritten to assert post-normalization output).

features.description: Update auditor finding-severity semantics so EC5 downgrade is **narrow**: only the specific case of missing-or-malformed prose prelude with a fully valid structured target_context. Every other EC5-shaped failure stays at `'i1'` (blocker). Change is two parts: (1) **Helper function** `classify_ec5_severity(envelope: dict) -> Literal['none', 'i0', 'i1']` in `scripts/jarvis_orchestrate/ec5_classifier.py`. Logic uses F001's `validate_target_context` + `parse_prelude_block` + `render_prelude`: (a) if `validate_target_context(envelope.target_context)` raises → return `'i1'` (struct invalid: missing target_context, empty env with commands, empty project with commands, commands without target metadata). (b) struct validates → call `parse_prelude_block(envelope.summary)`. (b.i) parse returns None (no prelude block detectable in summary) → return `'i0'` (format-only — prelude is missing; F002 would inject it, auditor finding is cosmetic). (b.ii) parse returns a dict and EVERY parsed value matches the rendered values from struct (Repo, Env, Project, Command-count) → return `'none'` (no finding to file; golden case). (b.iii) parse returns a dict but ANY parsed value mismatches the struct → return `'i1'` (auditor caught a real value-mismatch — content correctness, not format). (b.iv) parse raises a `prelude-shape` mismatch (looks like a prelude but malformed: wrong field order, mistyped labels, missing line) → return `'i0'` (format-only — F002 will normalize on next persist). **The downgrade fires ONLY in cases (b.i) and (b.iv).** (2) **Auditor prompt template** at `scripts/jarvis_orchestrate/prompts.py` gains a documented EC5 rule paragraph: 'EC5 (target-context prelude): file i1 ONLY when (i) target_context is missing, has empty/invalid env or project alongside non-empty commands_run, or commands_run is non-empty without target metadata; OR (ii) the prose prelude is present but its values disagree with the structured target_context (e.g. prelude says env=prod, struct says env=dev). For a missing or structurally-malformed prelude with VALID struct, file at most i0 — the platform writer will inject the canonical prelude on next persist, so the format gap is transient. NEVER downgrade based on struct validity alone; value-mismatches are real findings.' (3) **Finding-aggregation downgrade** is the platform's defensive layer (D005): after the auditor returns findings, scan for any with `code: EC5` (or text matching `target.context.prelude` heuristic for legacy outputs); for each, call `classify_ec5_severity(envelope)` and: if classifier returns `'none'` → drop the finding; `'i0'` → set finding.severity = 'i0' AND preserve description verbatim (D008); `'i1'` → leave as-is. (4) **End-to-end regression test**: case-a (post-F002) → 0 EC5 findings; case-c → 0 EC5 findings; case-d/e/f → 1 EC5 i1 finding each; **case-g → 1 EC5 i1 finding** (prelude value-mismatch, narrow rule). The classifier inspects only the structured + parsed-prelude state of the envelope; it doesn't second-guess auditor finding text. Description is preserved on every downgrade per D008.
steps: Add `scripts/jarvis_orchestrate/ec5_classifier.py` with `classify_ec5_severity(envelope) -> Literal['none', 'i0', 'i1']`. Pure function: takes a parsed envelope dict, returns a severity label. No I/O.

Logic: try `validate_target_context(envelope.get('target_context'))` — on raise return `'i1'`. On success: check `summary.lstrip().startswith(render_prelude(target_context).rstrip())` — if true return `'none'`, else return `'i0'`.

Wire into the auditor's finding-aggregation step: after the auditor returns its findings list but before `audit_writer` persists, scan findings for any with `code: EC5` (or text matching `target.context.prelude` heuristic for legacy auditor outputs that don't tag a code). For each, call `classify_ec5_severity(envelope)` and: if classifier returns `'none'`, drop the finding entirely; if `'i0'`, set finding.severity = 'i0' (preserve description); if `'i1'`, leave as-is.

Update the auditor prompt template (`prompts.py` AUDITOR_PROMPT or the equivalent template constant) to include the EC5 rule paragraph documented in the description. Paragraph is added to the existing 'severity classification' section (or a new section if none exists), framed as a rule the auditor follows; no agent retraining.

Tests — classifier parametrized over six F001 fixtures: case-a (post-F002 prelude injection) → `'none'`; case-a (raw, pre-injection) → `'i0'`; case-b → mirrors case-a behavior; case-c (golden) → `'none'`; case-d, case-e, case-f → all `'i1'`.

Tests — finding-aggregation downgrade: synthetic auditor output with one EC5 i1 finding + envelope-state matching case-c → finding dropped, aggregated list is empty. Same input but envelope matches case-a-raw → finding severity becomes i0, description preserved.
Tests — non-EC5 findings pass through: synthetic auditor output with one EC5 i1 + one S101 i1 + envelope-state matching case-c → only the EC5 finding is dropped, the S101 finding survives unchanged.
Tests — prompt template smoke: load AUDITOR_PROMPT, assert it contains the documented EC5 rule paragraph (string match on a short phrase like 'do NOT file an i1 EC5 finding').

Integration test — fresh volley regression: dispatch a synthetic volley iteration with the changelog-skill regression envelope (the recent EC5 i1 example sourced into F001 fixtures); assert post-F002+F003 the volley produces zero EC5 i1 findings (case-a-equivalent behavior). Same dispatch with case-d-shaped envelope produces exactly one EC5 i1 finding.
features.acceptance: (1) `scripts/jarvis_orchestrate/ec5_classifier.py` exists with `classify_ec5_severity(envelope)` exported; pure function, no I/O. (2) Classifier returns the documented severity for each of the **seven** F001 fixtures: case-a-pre-injection → 'i0' (missing prelude); case-a-post-injection / case-b-post-injection / case-c → 'none' (golden); case-d / case-e / case-f → 'i1' (struct invalid); **case-g → 'i1'** (struct valid BUT parsed prelude value mismatches struct — narrow rule). Verified by parametrized test. (3) **Narrow downgrade scope (D005 + acceptance-locked here)**: the classifier returns 'i0' ONLY when (a) struct validates AND (b) the summary either has no detectable prelude OR has a structurally-malformed prelude (wrong field order, mistyped labels, missing line). The classifier returns 'i1' in EVERY other case where an auditor would file EC5: missing struct, invalid struct (empty env/project with commands), commands-without-target, AND prelude-value-mismatch. Verified by a parametrized test with at least 6 negative-control cases (one per i1 trigger including value-mismatch). (4) Auditor finding-aggregation step calls the classifier on every EC5-coded finding and drops/downgrades per the classifier's verdict. (5) **Description preservation (D008)**: when the classifier downgrades severity, the original finding's `description` text is preserved verbatim in the persisted envelope; only `severity` is mutated. Verified by a test that asserts deep-equality on description before/after downgrade. (6) Auditor prompt template at `prompts.py` (or equivalent) contains the documented EC5 rule paragraph including the value-mismatch carve-out (`prelude says env=X, struct says env=Y` stays i1); verified by string-match test on a representative phrase. (7) Non-EC5 findings pass through the aggregation step unchanged — verified by mixed-finding test (one EC5 i1 + one S101 i1; only the EC5 is touched). (8) Integration test: a fresh synthetic volley iteration against a case-a-shaped envelope (post-F002 normalization) produces ZERO EC5 i1 findings; against case-d-shaped produces exactly one EC5 i1; against **case-g produces exactly one EC5 i1** (negative control — narrow rule respected). (9) No agent retraining — the only changes are (a) the classifier helper, (b) the prompt template paragraph addition, (c) finding-aggregation wiring. No model-tuning, no fine-tuning, no per-agent customization. (10) Backwards-compat: legacy auditor outputs that file EC5-shaped findings without a `code` field but with text matching the `target.context.prelude` heuristic are also handled by the aggregation downgrade — verified by a test using a synthetic legacy-shaped finding. (11) All existing orchestrate test modules stay green.
